## Data Preparation

```{r load library, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(here)
library(rio)
library(janitor)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r read in data, echo=FALSE}
###read in the approved data subset
data_raw <- import(here("data","NWS24_subset_edst676.csv")) |> 
  clean_names()

###pre-processing
pattern <- "^\\s*\\((\\d+)\\)\\s*"

data <- data_raw |>
  mutate(across(-c(age,lad_now,lad_fut),
    list(
      code  = ~ as.integer(str_match(as.character(.x), pattern)[, 2]),
      label = ~ str_remove(as.character(.x), pattern)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
  )) |>
  select(c(age,sex_code:metstat_self_label,lad_now, lad_fut, happy_code:intendvote_2024_label))
```

### Data Cleaning

1.  Remove observations with non-valid responses

```{r, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
#examine unique values and response frequencies
lapply(data |> select(ends_with("_code")), unique)
lapply(data |> select(ends_with("_code")), table, useNA="ifany")
summary(data |> select(age, lad_now, lad_fut))
sum(is.na(data |> select(age, lad_now, lad_fut)))
table(data$lad_now, useNA = "ifany")

#Recode missing values
nonmissing_data <- data |> 
  mutate(
    across(ends_with("_code"), ~ replace(.x, .x %in% c(98,99), NA_integer_)),
    lad_now = na_if(lad_now, 99)
  )

#check missing value recoding
colSums(is.na(nonmissing_data))
lapply(nonmissing_data |> select(ends_with("_code")), table, useNA="ifany")
summary(nonmissing_data |> select(age, lad_now, lad_fut))

#Remove observations with missing values
complete_data <- nonmissing_data |> 
  drop_na(ends_with("_code"), lad_now, lad_fut, age)
```

After recoding non-substantive responses as mssing values, we excluded participants with missing on any of the selected variables. A totoal of `r nrow(nonmissing_data)-nrow(complete_data)` observations with missing values were removed, resulting in a final sample of `r nrow(complete_data)` observations.

2.  compute composite scores

```{r, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
complete_data <- complete_data |> 
  mutate(
    #life satisfaction (5-25)
    life_sat = sat1_code + sat2_code +sat3_code+sat4_code+sat5_code,
    #reverse-code negatively worded resilience items
    res2_rev = 6- res2_code,
    res4_rev = 6- res4_code,
    res6_rev = 6- res6_code,
    #resilience (6-30)
    resilience=res1_code+res2_rev+res3_code+res4_rev+res5_code+res6_rev,
    #loneliness(3-9)
    loneliness=lonely_a_code+lonely_b_code+lonely_c_code
  )
#check sum scores
summary(complete_data |> select(life_sat, resilience, loneliness))
```

To facilitate subsequent analyses, we computed three composite scores: life satisfaction, resilience, and loneliness. Also, we reverse-coded three negatively worded items in resilience before summation.

### Data visualizations

1.  Resilience scores

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#Distribution in general
ggplot(complete_data, aes(x=resilience))+
  geom_bar(
    width = 1,
    fill = "lightblue"
  )+
  labs(
    title="Distribution of Resilience Scores",
    x="Resilience Score",
    y="Frequency"
  )+
  theme_minimal()

#Resilience by sex
ggplot(complete_data, aes(x=sex_label, y=resilience))+
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue")+
  labs(
    title = "Resilience by Sex",
    x="Sex",
    y="Resilience Score"
  )+
  theme_minimal()
  
#Resilience by Race/ethnicity
ggplot(complete_data, aes(x=racerec_label, y=resilience))+
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue")+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(
    title = "Resilience by Race/Ethnicity",
    x = "Race/Ethnicity",
    y = "Reslience Score"
  )+
  theme_minimal()
```
